children: Coca-Cola

is taking over beverage supply at KFC restaurants across the U.S., marking the first time the fast-food chain will serve Coke products nationwide and giving the company another symbolic win over longtime rival PepsiCo
The rollout is expected to cover all U.S. KFC locations by the spring.
TD Cowen analyst Robert Moskow called the deal positive for Coca-Cola, though he sees the direct financial impact as relatively modest.
The firm estimates the KFC contract could add roughly
10 to 20 basis points to Coca-Cola's total revenue in 2027
once the agreement takes effect.
The bigger story, in TD Cowen's view, is market share.
Moskow said Coca-Cola has gained about
70 basis points of U.S. carbonated soft-drink share over the past two years
, while PepsiCo has lost roughly
130 basis points
over the same period.
Keurig Dr Pepper has also gained share when energy drinks are included.
That leads TD Cowen to view PepsiCo's North American beverage business as a continuing
share donor
to Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper.

Moskow argues Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper have been investing more aggressively and consistently behind U.S. beverage growth, while PepsiCo has spent more time emphasizing cost reductions and margin expansion.
Investor Takeaway
I think the KFC win matters less because of the immediate revenue contribution and more because of what it potentially signals.
A 10 to 20 basis point boost to Coca-Cola's revenue is not transformational on its own.
But taking a major restaurant account from PepsiCo while simultaneously gaining retail share supports TD Cowen's argument that Coca-Cola has stronger momentum in North America.
For PepsiCo, the concern is whether KFC becomes another example of a broader competitive problem rather than an isolated contract loss.
For investors, the key things to watch are
U.S. beverage market share, restaurant-account wins, volume trends and whether PepsiCo can stabilize its North American beverage business
If Coca-Cola keeps taking share both at retail and in foodservice, the KFC deal could ultimately matter more as a signal than as a revenue event.

title: Coca-Cola Makes a Major Move With Fast-Food Giant KFC
